Memorandum from Division of Air Hazardour Materials to EOEA
Three concerns of the DAHM have been discussed above:
1. Relationship of proposed project to the BTCP,
2. Emission reductions attributed to motor vehicle emission inspection and maintenance program.
3. Application of appropriate pollutant emission factors.
The fourth concern presented by the DAHM regards the vehicle mile travel projections and emission estimates.
The first and most important point to make with regard to DAHM's comment is that the environmental impact statement did not attempt to identify total regionwide vehicles miles traveled. There were two statements made in the DEIS which could have been interpreted as implying that total regional VMT was being predicted:
"In the other major categories of vehicle trips, those generated by service, visitors, and business activities of the development, there are several factors that suggest a stabilized if not reduced VMT".
"In summary, it is concluded that the total VMT generated within the region would be reduced by the project."
These sentences are found on page 69, of Chapter 5 of Part II. In addition, on pages 1-6 of the Air Quality Analysis, the following statement is made: "This transportation analysis indicates that, by virtue of the project location (i.e., near mass transportation) and the high employee-to-parking ratio, regional vehicle miles traveled (VMT) will remain constant or possibly, decrease with implementation of any of the build alternatives."
What was intended by these statements and what should appear evident by the context in which the statements are made, is that the change in regional VMT occurring as a result of the proposed Kendall Square Project would be either zero or something of a reduction. This is not to say that the total vehicle miles traveled within the Creater Metropolitan Boston area will either stay the same or decrease because of the Kendall Square Project.
